first.text:
Nothing in the sessions themselves. Every set, rep, load and rest on Wednesday, Friday and Sunday stays exactly as it is: the scapular pulls, the negatives, the band pull-ups, the flexed-arm hang, the strict single on Friday. Each line still progresses the way it did (reps up inside its range, then a lighter band or a longer lower). You won't do anything different this week or next because of it.

What changes is how the week is judged afterwards, and that has three practical effects:

1. **Your pull-up work finally counts.** Until now the only pull-up work that counted toward the lift's weekly target was the one strict single, so the ten sets of negatives and band pull-ups you do each week were invisible to the weekly dose check. Now they count. A full week shows 11 hard sets against a target of 10.

2. **A lost Wednesday gets noticed.** If a late night takes out Wednesday, the week shows 4 sets against 10. If that happens three weeks out of four, the check-in will tell us the pull-up is behind, and I'll propose where the missing sets go back (a band set added to Sunday, or Wednesday's work shifted to Thursday). Before this, a missed Wednesday looked exactly like a full week.

3. **A cut-down week keeps pull-up work.** When a week is disrupted and we plan the bare minimum, each priority lift must keep at least two hard sets. Negatives and band pull-ups now satisfy that for the pull-up, so a minimum week can carry two sets of negatives instead of forcing strict attempts you can't yet make.

Two things it doesn't change: the Friday strict single is still the only test of the lift, and negatives or band pull-ups never stand in for it. And the pull-up target still plays no part in your other lifts.

The draft is ready as described; say yes and I'll adopt it.
